# Rivers of the world and their mouths — provenance report

<!-- Generated from authored/world-rivers.json by scripts/authored_decks.py. Do not edit: change the dossier and rebuild. -->

**Deck:** [`decks/world-rivers.ttl`](../decks/world-rivers.ttl) · **Cards:** 50 · **Licence:** [CC0 1.0 Universal](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) · **Compiled by:** Anton Wiklund · **Created:** 2026-10-04

50 major rivers of the world and the water each one flows into: a sea, ocean, bay, lake or another river. The rivers come from every continent except Antarctica, seven of them Nordic, such as the Torne and the Göta älv. Front: the river; back: where it flows into, in English and Swedish. The mouth is a water that Wikidata records for the river (P403); where it records several, the card gives the sea or bay that the other sources also name, sometimes with a note. Rivers whose mouth is disputed or splits between different waters are left out. From Wikidata, checked against Wikipedia and Nationalencyklopedin.

## Licensing

The content sources are Wikidata, whose structured data is CC0, and Executive Order 14172, a work of the US Government and not under copyright: the mouths, the English and Swedish names and the facts in the notes come from them, so the deck is CC0 1.0 like the rest of the library. The choice of 50 rivers is the compiler's own, not taken from any list. The English and Swedish Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0) and Nationalencyklopedin (all rights reserved) were used for verification only: they confirmed the mouths and the Swedish names that Wikidata gave, and no wording, list or selection was copied from them. The Swedish forms Darlingfloden, Murrayfloden and Bohaihavet, compared with Wikipedia and NE, are Swedish aliases in Wikidata. One Swedish place name in a note, "Jenisejviken", is not in Wikidata and was taken from the Swedish Wikipedia; a single name is a fact, not a copyrightable expression, so it does not bring in the CC BY-SA licence. The fronts, backs and notes are the compiler's own wording of facts.

## Method

1. Who did the work: Anton Wiklund compiled this deck with the help of AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic), which did the research, drafting and cross-checking at his direction. The cards were checked by machine (live Wikidata and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators) and in independent review rounds by further Claude agents, each logged under Quality control with its findings and how they were resolved. Anton Wiklund reviews every deck in full before it is released.
2. 1. Candidates (query 1): a list of 99 rivers, written by the compiler to cover every continent and the Nordic countries and including well-known tributaries, was looked up in Wikidata by the titles of their English Wikipedia articles, with every P403 (mouth of the watercourse) statement, its rank and the English and Swedish labels of river and mouth. Rivers whose English article title did not match (the Torne, Ob, Yenisei, Lena, St. Lawrence, Ångermanälven, Tana and Kymijoki) were looked up by their Swedish article titles (query 2). The Lena has no P403 statement and was dropped.
3. 2. Selection: from the candidates the compiler chose 50 rivers whose mouth is one named water that every source checked agrees on (see Selection). For each, query 4 fetched every P403 statement with its rank, and query 3 every English, Swedish and multilingual (mul) label and alias of the rivers and of the waters they flow into. Query 6 fetched P361 (part of), P403, P200 (inflows) and P31 (instance of) of some of the waters, for the notes; query 7 checked whether any Wikidata item records the Gulf of Ob as the Ob's mouth (none does).
4. 3. The back of each card is the value of the river's P403 statement. Where Wikidata gives more than one value (Elbe: North Sea, German Bight, Heligoland Bight; Loire: Bay of Biscay, Loire estuary; Yenisei: Kara Sea, Yenisei Gulf; Volga: Caspian Sea, Kama), the card names the one item that is a sea, ocean, bay or lake in its own right and that the other sources also name, and a note may name a narrower water (Elbe: German Bight; Yenisei: Yenisei Gulf) or the wider one (Loire: Atlantic Ocean); the Volga card has no note. The Volga's second value, the Kama, is its tributary, not its mouth (see quality control).
5. 4. Names: the English front is the river's short English name ("Danube", "Amazon", "Mississippi"); "River" is kept only where it is part of the name ("Yellow River", "Orange River"), and the Nordic rivers keep their own names as English does ("Göta älv", "Kemijoki"). The English back is the Wikidata English label of the water, except "Gulf of St. Lawrence" (an English alias, matching the front "St. Lawrence"), "Mississippi" and "Murray" (short forms, matching the fronts). The Swedish front and back are the Wikidata Swedish label, or, where Swedish reference works use another established form, a Swedish alias: Darlingfloden (the title of the Swedish Wikipedia article and NE's headword; the Swedish label is "Darling"), Murrayfloden (the form NE uses in its article on the Darling, matching "Darlingfloden" on the same card; the Swedish label is "Murray") and Bohaihavet (the form in the text of the Swedish Wikipedia article on the Yellow River; the Swedish label is "Bohai"). Every Swedish name was compared with the title of the river's Swedish Wikipedia article and with NE's headword or alternative names. NE's headwords for the Yangtze and the Yellow River are "Chang Jiang" and "Huang He" (NE gives "Gula floden" as another name); the cards use the Swedish Wikipedia's and Wikidata's "Yangtze" and "Gula floden" and give the Chinese names in a note. "Saint Lawrencefloden" and "Saint Lawrenceviken" follow the Wikidata Swedish labels, the Swedish Wikipedia and NE, not the hyphenated alias "Saint Lawrence-floden". The notes' Swedish water names are Wikidata Swedish labels, except "Jenisejviken" (Yenisei Gulf), which has no Swedish label or alias in Wikidata and was taken from the Swedish Wikipedia article "Jenisej" (infobox and text).
6. 5. Wikipedia check: the current English and Swedish Wikipedia article of every river (titles from the Wikidata sitelinks, query 5) was fetched with its revision id through the MediaWiki API (fetch_wiki.py and fetch_wiki2.py), and the infobox fields mouth, mouth_location and mynning and the sentences of the text that name the mouth were extracted (mouths.py, which replaces templates such as unit conversions with "…" and removes link markup and references). The card table <scratch>/cards.py holds, for each card, only values that appear in the dossier: the Wikidata items of river and mouth, the names on the card, the notes, the Wikipedia article keys, the NE address and the marker string that picks the quoted sentence. The script make_cards.py (query 14) then wrote the evidence of every card from these extracts and from the saved Wikidata results; the compiler chose for each article the sentence to quote and read every card's evidence against the article.
7. 6. NE check: the article of each river on Nationalencyklopedin (ne.se) was fetched (fetch_ne.py) and the opening shown to visitors without a subscription was read. Article addresses were guessed from the Swedish names; where that failed (Po, Kongo, Niger) a web search on ne.se found the address form "kongo-(flod-afrika)". No NE article was found for the Paraná or the São Francisco, whose cards rest on Wikidata and the two Wikipedias. Britannica was tried first and answered 403 to the research environment: curl -s -A "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -L -o <scratch>/brit-danube.html -w "%{http_code} %{url_effective} %{size_download}\n" https://www.britannica.com/place/Danube-River; it was not used.
8. 7. Mississippi note: the text of Executive Order 14172 was downloaded from the Government Publishing Office (govinfo.gov) and its Sec. 4 read; the note states only what the order did in January 2025, not the name's later use.
9. 8. Machine checks: for every card the builder checks against live Wikidata that the river has the P403 value on the back, and that the English and Swedish names on the card are labels or aliases of the river and of the water in that language or in Wikidata's multilingual (mul) set, where they are ("Torne" and "Congo" are mul labels and "Mississippi" a mul alias, not English ones; no English or mul label or alias matches the short English names Mekong, Irrawaddy, Columbia, Mackenzie, Amazon, Paraná, Magdalena, Darling and Murray, which have no label check). make_dossier.py assembled this dossier from cards.json and the text written for it. The notes rest on the Wikidata statements and the order named in each card's evidence. The built deck was validated with the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators (validate_sources.ts).

## Selection

50 rivers: 13 in the rest of Europe (Danube, Rhine, Volga, Don, Elbe, Thames, Seine, Loire, Rhône, Po, Tagus, Tiber, and the Ural, conventionally counted as the Europe–Asia boundary along much of its lower course), 7 Nordic (Göta älv, Klarälven, Torne, Kemijoki, Oulujoki, Vuoksi, Kymijoki), 9 in Asia, 8 in Africa, 7 in North America, 5 in South America and 1 in Australia, chosen by the compiler among the world's best-known rivers, with a few well-known tributaries (Blue and White Nile, Missouri, Darling) and rivers flowing into lakes (Klarälven, Vuoksi, Niagara, Jordan). The mouth is a water named by the river's P403 statement in Wikidata (the Loire into the Bay of Biscay, the Torne into the Bothnian Bay, not the Atlantic or the Gulf of Bothnia). Where Wikidata names several waters (the Elbe, Loire and Yenisei), the card gives the sea or bay that the other sources also name (the North Sea, the Bay of Biscay, the Kara Sea) and the note names the narrower or wider water; a river that joins another flows into that river. Left out because sources name different waters as the mouth or the river ends in several: the Ob (Wikidata: Kara Sea; Wikipedia and NE: the Gulf of Ob), Dalälven (Wikidata: Gävle Bay; Swedish Wikipedia: the Bothnian Sea; English Wikipedia: the Gulf of Bothnia), the Glomma (Wikidata and the Wikipedia infoboxes: Skagerrak; the texts: the Oslofjord), the Vistula (a delta into Gdańsk Bay and the Vistula Lagoon), the Oder (Wikidata: Baltic Sea and Szczecin Lagoon), the Dnieper and Dniester (estuaries ranked above or instead of the Black Sea) and the Kama (Wikidata: the Volga, the Kuybyshev Reservoir and the Chusovaya). Left out because Wikidata names no mouth: the Lena. Left out because their Wikidata mouth is a little-known local water (Lule älv, Ume älv, Indalsälven, Kalix älv, Motala ström, the Neva, the Northern Dvina, the Hudson, the Pechora). Left out to keep the deck at about 50 and avoid repeating the same back: the Amur, Brahmaputra, Kolyma, Yalu, Tigris, Amu Darya, Syr Darya, Murray, Colorado, Rio Grande, Ohio, Uruguay, Senegal, Douro, Guadalquivir, Weser, Main, Moselle, Inn, Daugava, Pite älv and others among the 99 candidates. Several big rivers end in a delta (Danube, Nile, Mekong, Ganges, Niger), but into one water, and are included. The Rhine's distributary IJssel flows into the IJsselmeer, but every source checked names the North Sea as the Rhine's mouth.

## Queries

**1. The 99 candidate rivers by English Wikipedia title, with every P403 value, rank and labels (sh <scratch>/run.sh q1, which runs: curl -s -H "User-Agent: solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -H "Accept: text/csv" --data-urlencode query@<scratch>/q1.rq https://query.wikidata.org/sparql > <scratch>/q1.csv)** (Wikidata: the mouth of the watercourse (P403) of each river, and the English and Swedish labels and aliases of the rivers and of the waters they flow into)

```
SELECT ?title ?river ?en ?sv ?mouth ?mouthEn ?mouthSv ?rank WHERE {
  VALUES ?title { "Danube"@en "Rhine"@en "Volga"@en "Dnieper"@en "Don (river)"@en "Elbe"@en "Vistula"@en "Oder"@en "River Thames"@en "Seine"@en "Loire"@en "Rhône"@en "Po (river)"@en "Tagus"@en "Ebro"@en "Daugava"@en "Neva"@en "Northern Dvina"@en "Ural (river)"@en "Tiber"@en "Torne (river)"@en "Göta älv"@en "Klarälven"@en "Dalälven"@en "Ångermanälven"@en "Glomma"@en "Kemijoki"@en "Motala ström"@en "Lule River"@en "Ume River"@en "Indalsälven"@en "Yangtze"@en "Yellow River"@en "Mekong"@en "Ob (river)"@en "Yenisey"@en "Lena (river)"@en "Amur"@en "Indus River"@en "Ganges"@en "Euphrates"@en "Tigris"@en "Jordan River"@en "Amu Darya"@en "Syr Darya"@en "Irrawaddy River"@en "Salween"@en "Nile"@en "Congo River"@en "Niger River"@en "Zambezi"@en "Limpopo River"@en "Orange River"@en "Senegal River"@en "Blue Nile"@en "White Nile"@en "Mississippi River"@en "Missouri River"@en "Ohio River"@en "Saint Lawrence River"@en "Colorado River"@en "Columbia River"@en "Yukon River"@en "Mackenzie River"@en "Rio Grande"@en "Hudson River"@en "Niagara River"@en "Amazon River"@en "Paraná River"@en "Orinoco"@en "Uruguay River"@en "São Francisco River"@en "Magdalena River"@en "Murray River"@en "Darling River"@en "Kama (river)"@en "Oka (river)"@en "Main (river)"@en "Moselle"@en "Inn (river)"@en "Douro"@en "Guadalquivir"@en "Dniester"@en "Pechora (river)"@en "Kolyma (river)"@en "Brahmaputra River"@en "Pearl River (China)"@en "Yalu River"@en "Shannon (river)"@en "Severn"@en "Weser"@en "Vuoksi"@en "Kymi (river)"@en "Oulujoki"@en "Tana (Norway)"@en "Numedalslågen"@en "Tanaelva"@en "Kalix River"@en "Pite River"@en }
  ?article schema:about ?river ; schema:isPartOf <https://en.wikipedia.org/> ; schema:name ?title .
  OPTIONAL { ?river p:P403 ?st . ?st ps:P403 ?mouth ; wikibase:rank ?rank .
    OPTIONAL { ?mouth rdfs:label ?mouthEn FILTER(LANG(?mouthEn) = "en") }
    OPTIONAL { ?mouth rdfs:label ?mouthSv FILTER(LANG(?mouthSv) = "sv") } }
  OPTIONAL { ?river rdfs:label ?en FILTER(LANG(?en) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?river rdfs:label ?sv FILTER(LANG(?sv) = "sv") }
}
ORDER BY ?title

```

```
import csv, collections, os, json
D = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
out = collections.defaultdict(lambda: collections.defaultdict(list))
```

**9. The English and Swedish Wikipedia articles with their revision ids (python3 <scratch>/fetch_wiki.py, then python3 <scratch>/fetch_wiki2.py for the Irrawaddy and the Oulujoki; extraction by python3 <scratch>/mouths.py)** (English Wikipedia: the article on each river (infobox and text))

```
"""Fetch the current wikitext and revision id of every river's English and Swedish
Wikipedia article (titles from q5.csv) through the MediaWiki API; write wiki.json."""
import csv, json, os, time, urllib.parse, urllib.request
D = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
UA = "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)"
titles = {}
for r in csv.DictReader(open(f"{D}/q5.csv", encoding="utf-8")):
    lang = "en" if "en.wikipedia" in r["wiki"] else "sv"
    titles.setdefault(lang, {})[r["title"]] = r["item"].rsplit("/", 1)[1]
out = {}
for lang, ts in titles.items():
    names = sorted(ts)
    for i in range(0, len(names), 25):
        chunk = names[i:i + 25]
        url = (f"https://{lang}.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=query&format=json&formatversion=2"
               "&prop=revisions&rvprop=ids|content&rvslots=main&titles=" + urllib.parse.quote("|".join(chunk)))
        # one revision per page is only allowed for a single title, so fetch one by one
        for t in chunk:
            u = (f"https://{lang}.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=query&format=json&formatversion=2"
                 "&prop=revisions&rvprop=ids|content&rvslots=main&titles=" + urllib.parse.quote(t))
            req = urllib.request.Request(u, headers={"User-Agent": UA})
            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as resp:
                page = json.load(resp)["query"]["pages"][0]
            rev = page["revisions"][0]
            out[f"{lang}:{t}"] = {"qid": ts[t], "lang": lang, "title": t, "revid": rev["revid"],
                                  "text": rev["slots"]["main"]["content"]}
            time.sleep(0.3)
json.dump(out, open(f"{D}/wiki.json", "w", encoding="utf-8"), ensure_ascii=False)
print(len(out), "articles")

# fetch_wiki2.py
"""Add the Irrawaddy and Oulujoki articles (en and sv) to wiki.json, then rerun mouths.py."""
import json, os, urllib.parse, urllib.request
D = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
UA = "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)"
want = [("en", "Irrawaddy River", "Q26076"), ("sv", "Irrawaddy", "Q26076"),
        ("en", "Oulujoki", "Q736575"), ("sv", "Ule älv", "Q736575")]
out = json.load(open(f"{D}/wiki.json", encoding="utf-8"))
for lang, t, q in want:
    u = (f"https://{lang}.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=query&format=json&formatversion=2&redirects=1"
         "&prop=revisions&rvprop=ids|content&rvslots=main&titles=" + urllib.parse.quote(t))
    with urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(u, headers={"User-Agent": UA}), timeout=60) as resp:
        page = json.load(resp)["query"]["pages"][0]
    rev = page["revisions"][0]
    out[f"{lang}:{page['title']}"] = {"qid": q, "lang": lang, "title": page["title"], "revid": rev["revid"],
                                      "text": rev["slots"]["main"]["content"]}
    print(lang, page["title"], rev["revid"])
json.dump(out, open(f"{D}/wiki.json", "w", encoding="utf-8"), ensure_ascii=False)

# mouths.py
"""Pull the infobox mouth fields and the first lead sentences naming the mouth out of wiki.json."""
import json, os, re
D = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
w = json.load(open(f"{D}/wiki.json", encoding="utf-8"))
FIELD = re.compile(r"^\s*\|\s*(mouth|mouth_location|mynning|mynningsort|mouth_name|mynning_namn|utlopp|river_mouth)\s*=\s*(.*)$", re.M | re.I)
SENT = re.compile(r"[^.\n]*\b(into|empties|discharges|mynnar|utmynnar|rinner ut|flows into|ut i|mouth|drains)\b[^.\n]*\.", re.I)
def clean(s):
    s = re.sub(r"<ref[^>]*/>", "", s)
    s = re.sub(r"<ref[^>]*>.*?</ref>", "", s, flags=re.S)
    s = re.sub(r"\{\{[^{}]*\}\}", "…", s)
    s = re.sub(r"\[\[(?:[^|\]]*\|)?([^\]]*)\]\]", r"\1", s)
    s = re.sub(r"'{2,}", "", s)
    return s.strip()
res = {}
for key, a in sorted(w.items(), key=lambda kv: (kv[1]["qid"], kv[0])):
    t = a["text"]
    fields = [(m.group(1), clean(m.group(2))) for m in FIELD.finditer(t)]
    body = re.sub(r"\{\{[^{}]*\}\}", "…", re.sub(r"\{\{[^{}]*\}\}", "…", t))
    lead = clean(body)[:6000]
    sents = [clean(m.group(0)) for m in SENT.finditer(lead)][:3]
    res[key] = {"qid": a["qid"], "revid": a["revid"], "fields": fields, "sentences": sents}
    print(f"{a['qid']} {key} rev {a['revid']}")
    for f in fields:
        print("   F", f)
    for s in sents:
        print("   S", s[:300])
json.dump(res, open(f"{D}/mouths.json", "w", encoding="utf-8"), ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)

```

```
# fetch_ne.py
"""Fetch the Nationalencyklopedin (ne.se) article of each river and print its headword,
definition and the first part of the text (the part shown to visitors). Saves ne/<slug>.html
and ne.json. Usage: python3 fetch_ne.py slug1 slug2 ..."""
import html, json, os, re, sys, time, urllib.parse, urllib.request
D = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
UA = "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)"
os.makedirs(f"{D}/ne", exist_ok=True)
try:
    store = json.load(open(f"{D}/ne.json", encoding="utf-8"))
except FileNotFoundError:
    store = {}
ARGS = sys.argv[1:]
if ARGS and ARGS[0] == "-f":
    ARGS = open(ARGS[1], encoding="utf-8").read().split()
for slug in ARGS:
    url = "https://www.ne.se/uppslagsverk/encyklopedi/l%C3%A5ng/" + urllib.parse.quote(slug)
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": UA})
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as resp:
            t = resp.read().decode("utf-8")
            code = resp.status
    except Exception as e:  # noqa
        print(slug, "ERROR", e)
        continue
    open(f"{D}/ne/{slug}.html", "w", encoding="utf-8").write(t)
    canon = re.findall(r'<link rel="canonical" href="([^"]+)"', t)
    i = t.find('<span class="huvud">')
    seg = t[i:i + 6000] if i >= 0 else ""
    seg = re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", seg)
    seg = html.unescape(re.sub(r"\s+", " ", seg)).strip()[:900]
    store[slug] = {"url": url, "status": code, "canonical": canon[-1] if canon else "", "text": seg}
    print(f"== {slug} {code} {canon[-1] if canon else ''}\n   {seg}")
    time.sleep(0.5)
json.dump(store, open(f"{D}/ne.json", "w", encoding="utf-8"), ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)

```

**14. The cards' evidence and checks were written from the saved results by python3 <scratch>/make_cards.py (card table in <scratch>/cards.py), the dossier by python3 <scratch>/make_dossier.py** (Wikidata: the mouth of the watercourse (P403) of each river, and the English and Swedish labels and aliases of the rivers and of the waters they flow into)

```
"""Build the cards (with evidence and checks) of the world-rivers dossier from the saved
query results: q3.csv/labels.json (Wikidata labels), q4.csv (Wikidata P403), mouths.json
(Wikipedia infobox fields and lead sentences), ne.json (Nationalencyklopedin). Writes cards.json."""
import csv, json, os, re, sys
D = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path.insert(0, D)
from cards import CARDS

R = "2026-10-04"
labels = json.load(open(f"{D}/labels.json", encoding="utf-8"))
p403 = {}
for r in csv.DictReader(open(f"{D}/q4.csv", encoding="utf-8")):
    q = r["river"].rsplit("/", 1)[1]
    m = r["mouth"].rsplit("/", 1)[1]
    p403.setdefault(q, [])
    if m not in [x[0] for x in p403[q]]:
        p403[q].append((m, r["rank"].rsplit("#", 1)[1]))
wiki = json.load(open(f"{D}/mouths.json", encoding="utf-8"))
wikitext = json.load(open(f"{D}/wiki.json", encoding="utf-8"))
ne = json.load(open(f"{D}/ne.json", encoding="utf-8"))
NOTE_FIX = {"elbe": ("Its estuary opens into the German Bight", "Dess mynningsvik öppnar sig mot Tyska bukten")}


def names(q, lang):
    d = labels.get(q, {})
    return set(d.get(f"{lang}-label", [])) | set(d.get(f"{lang}-alias", [])) | set(d.get("mul-label", [])) | set(d.get("mul-alias", []))


def label(q, lang):
    d = labels.get(q, {})
    return (d.get(f"{lang}-label") or d.get("mul-label") or ["(none)"])[0]


def wiki_says(key, marker):
    a = wiki[key]
    parts = []
    for f, v in a["fields"]:
        if f not in ("mouth", "mouth_location", "mynning"):
            continue
        bits = re.split(r"\s*\|\s*", v.replace("{{ubl", "").strip())
        named = [(f, bits[0])] + [tuple(x.split("=", 1)) for x in bits[1:] if "=" in x]
        for name, val in named:
            name, val = name.strip(), val.strip().replace(" (…)", "")
            if val and val != "…" and name.startswith(("mouth", "mynning")) and not name.endswith(("_d", "_m", "_s", "coordinates", "_land")):
                parts.append(f"infobox {name} = {val}")
    if marker:
        hits = [s for s in a["sentences"] if marker in s]
        if not hits:
            # search the whole cleaned text
            text = wikitext[key]["text"]
            text = re.sub(r"<ref[^>]*/>", "", text)
            text = re.sub(r"<ref[^>]*>.*?</ref>", "", text, flags=re.S)
            text = re.sub(r"\[\[(?:[^|\]]*\|)?([^\]]*)\]\]", r"\1", text)
            text = re.sub(r"'{2,}", "", text)
            m = re.search(r"[^.\n]*" + re.escape(marker) + r"[^.\n]*\.?", text)
            hits = [m.group(0).strip()] if m else []
        if not hits:
            raise SystemExit(f"{key}: marker {marker!r} not found")
        h = hits[0].replace("&nbsp;", " ")
        h = re.sub(r"\{\{[^{}]*\}\}", "…", h)
        h = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", h).strip()
        if h[0].islower():
            h = "… " + h
        parts.append(f"text: \"{h}\"")
    if not parts:
        raise SystemExit(f"{key}: nothing to quote")
    return "; ".join(parts)


def ne_says(slug, marker):
    t = ne[slug]["text"]
    t = t.split(" Information om artikeln")[0]
    t = re.sub(r"\s+([,.;:)])", r"\1", t)
    t = t.replace("( ", "(")
    if marker is None:
        return None
    sents = re.split(r"(?<=[.])\s+(?=[A-ZÅÄÖ])", t)
    hits = [s for s in sents if marker in s]
    if not hits:
        raise SystemExit(f"NE {slug}: {marker!r} not found in {t!r}")
    return hits[0].strip()


cards = []
for (cid, q, mq, fen, fsv, ben, bsv, enk, svk, enm, svm, neslug, nem, nen, nsv) in CARDS:
    if cid in NOTE_FIX:
        nen, nsv = NOTE_FIX[cid]
    mouths = p403[q]
    assert mq in [m for m, _ in mouths], (cid, mouths)
    wd_mouths = "; ".join(f"P403 (mouth of the watercourse) {m} (en \"{label(m, 'en')}\", sv \"{label(m, 'sv')}\"), {rank.replace('Rank', '').lower()} rank"
                          for m, rank in mouths)
    says = (f"{wd_mouths}; river labels: en \"{label(q, 'en')}\", sv \"{label(q, 'sv')}\"")
    extra = []
    if fen not in names(q, "en"):
        extra.append(f"\"{fen}\" is not an English label or alias")
    else:
        if fen != label(q, "en"):
            extra.append(f"English alias \"{fen}\"")
    if fsv != label(q, "sv") and fsv in names(q, "sv"):
        extra.append(f"Swedish alias \"{fsv}\"")
    if bsv != label(mq, "sv") and bsv in names(mq, "sv"):
        extra.append(f"Swedish alias of {mq} \"{bsv}\"")
    if extra:
        says += "; " + "; ".join(extra)
    ev = [{"source": "wikidata", "locator": f"{q} ({label(q, 'en')}), P403 (query 4) and labels and aliases (query 3)",
           "says": says, "retrieved": R}]
    ev.append({"source": "wikipedia-en",
               "locator": f"\"{wikitext[enk]['title']}\", revision {wikitext[enk]['revid']}: https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid={wikitext[enk]['revid']}",
               "says": wiki_says(enk, enm), "retrieved": R})
    ev.append({"source": "wikipedia-sv",
               "locator": f"\"{wikitext[svk]['title']}\", revision {wikitext[svk]['revid']}: https://sv.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid={wikitext[svk]['revid']}",
               "says": wiki_says(svk, svm), "retrieved": R})
    if neslug:
        head = ne_says(neslug, ne[neslug]["text"].split(",")[0].split(" [")[0]) if False else None
        t = ne[neslug]["text"].split(" Information om artikeln")[0]
        t = re.sub(r"\s+([,.;:)])", r"\1", t)
        first = t.split(". ")[0] + "."
        first = re.sub(r" \[[^\]]*\]", "", first)
        s = ne_says(neslug, nem) if nem else first
        ev.append({"source": "ne", "locator": f"Nationalencyklopedin, \"{ne[neslug]['canonical'].rsplit('/', 1)[1]}\" ({ne[neslug]['url']}), the opening shown to visitors",
                   "says": s, "retrieved": R})
    if cid == "mississippi":
        ev.append({"source": "eo-14172", "locator": "Executive Order 14172 of January 20, 2025, Sec. 4 (a), Federal Register vol. 90, no. 20, p. 8629",
                   "says": "Sec. 4. Gulf of America. (a) The area formerly known as the Gulf of Mexico … I am directing that it officially be renamed the Gulf of America.",
                   "retrieved": R})
    checks = [{"qid": q, "property": "P403", "expect": mq}]
    for lang, text, item in (("en", fen, q), ("sv", fsv, q), ("en", ben, mq), ("sv", bsv, mq)):
        if text in names(item, lang):
            checks.append({"qid": item, "label": lang, "equals": text})
    card = {"id": cid, "front": {"en": fen, "sv": fsv}, "back": {"en": ben, "sv": bsv}}
    if nen:
        card["backNote"] = {"en": nen, "sv": nsv}
    card["evidence"] = ev
    card["checks"] = checks
    cards.append(card)
    missing = [(l, t) for l, t, i in (("en", fen, q), ("sv", fsv, q), ("en", ben, mq), ("sv", bsv, mq)) if t not in names(i, l)]
    if missing:
        print(cid, "no label check for", missing)
json.dump(cards, open(f"{D}/cards.json", "w", encoding="utf-8"), ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
print(len(cards), "cards")

```

## Quality control

6 rounds, 31 findings: 24 fixed, 0 rejected after checking, 7 needing no change. Every card's Wikidata checks (241 in all) are re-run against live Wikidata by `scripts/authored_decks.py check` before every build.

### Round 0: Sources, licences and machine checks: every card's mouth against Wikidata (P403), the English and Swedish Wikipedia and Nationalencyklopedin; the Swedish names against Wikidata sv labels, the Swedish Wikipedia and NE; the build's live Wikidata checks. (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — authoring agent, machine checks · **Scope:** All 50 cards, the 99 candidate rivers, the sources and the deck metadata.

For all 50 rivers Wikidata's P403, the English and Swedish Wikipedia and (where it says) NE name the same water, or a narrower or wider name for it (Torne: Bothnian Bay or Gulf of Bothnia; Loire: Bay of Biscay or Atlantic; Mackenzie: Beaufort Sea or Arctic Ocean). Two Swedish Wikipedia infoboxes are wrong and their texts right. No Wikidata check was skipped. Candidates with a disputed or split mouth were left out.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| volga | Wikidata gives the Volga two P403 values: the Caspian Sea and the Kama. The Kama is the Volga's tributary (the Kama's own P403 is the Volga), so the second value is an error in Wikidata. | The card follows the Caspian Sea value, which the English and Swedish Wikipedia and NE confirm; the builder checks that value. The Kama value is recorded in the card's evidence. | no change needed |

Recorded in the evidence. | no change needed |

### Round 1: Factual accuracy (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — independent Factual accuracy reviewer · **Scope:** All 50 cards against live Wikidata (P403, labels, aliases, mul) and general geography; counts and the description.

No card's mouth was found wrong and every check passes. The description's "as precisely as Wikidata names it" did not match the Elbe, Yenisei and Loire cards; the Swedish "Murray" broke the deck's naming style; "Don" and "Jordan" got disambiguating front notes; method and evidence called mul labels and aliases English.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| deck | The description and selection say the mouth is given "as precisely as Wikidata names it", but Wikidata's P403 also names the German Bight and Heligoland Bight (Elbe), the Yenisei Gulf (Yenisei) and the Loire estuary (Loire), while the cards give the North Sea, Kara Sea and Bay of Biscay. Confirmed with wbgetentities today. | Description (en, sv) and selection reworded to the rule actually applied: the mouth is a water Wikidata records under P403; where it records several, the card gives the sea or bay the other sources also name, and a note names the narrower water. The cards are unchanged; their notes already name the German Bight and the Yenisei Gulf. | fixed |
| darling | The Swedish back "Murray" does not match the "-floden" style of the front "Darlingfloden"; NE's Darling article says "Murrayfloden", a Swedish alias of Q183078 (confirmed today). | Swedish back changed to "Murrayfloden"; the sv label check on Q183078 now expects "Murrayfloden" (passes as an alias); evidence, method step 4 and licensing updated. | fixed |
| don | "Don" also names rivers in Scotland and England; the front could be read as ambiguous. | frontNote "In Russia" / "I Ryssland" added to the don card, and "In the Middle East" / "I Mellanöstern" to the jordan card (a Jordan River also flows into the Great Salt Lake in Utah). | fixed |
| deck | Method step 8 says the names are checked as English labels or aliases, but "Torne" and "Congo" pass only as mul labels and "Mississippi" (Mississippi front and Missouri back) only as a mul alias; the mississippi evidence called it an English alias. Confirmed with wbgetentities (languages en\|sv\|mul) today. | Method step 8 now says labels or aliases in that language or the multilingual (mul) set and names the three mul cases; the torne, congo and mississippi evidence now say mul label/alias, and the missouri evidence notes that its back is a mul alias. | fixed |

### Round 2: Language, translation and language tags (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — independent Language, translation and language tags reviewer · **Scope:** All 50 cards and the deck metadata: Swedish names and idiom, English wording, language tags, keywords.

Tags, keywords and Swedish names were sound. Fixed: the Darling card's mixed Swedish naming, the word order of the Mississippi note, the dangling subject of the Euphrates note, the Swedish description's P403 gloss and the English documentation's Swedish forms of Finnish and Torne names. The unhyphenated Saint Lawrence compounds are kept and now documented.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| darling | Front "Darlingfloden" and back "Murray" use two naming styles on one card. | Back sv changed to "Murrayfloden", a Wikidata Swedish alias and NE's form (see round 1). | fixed |
| mississippi | The Swedish note splits the particle verb ("Döptes … om"); "presidentorder" is the more usual term. | backNote.sv now "Döptes om till Gulf of America för amerikanskt federalt bruk genom en presidentorder i januari 2025". | fixed |
| euphrates | The note's subject dangles in English ("Formed where it meets the Tigris") and is missing in Swedish. | Notes now "The Shatt al-Arab forms where the Euphrates meets the Tigris, and flows into the Persian Gulf" / "Shatt al-Arab bildas där Eufrat möter Tigris och mynnar i Persiska viken". | fixed |
| deck | The Swedish description glosses P403 as "mynning" (Wikidata's sv label is "mynnar i", confirmed today) and repeats "anger" and "så". | Swedish description rewritten with the round-1 rule: "Mynningen är ett vatten som Wikidata anger för floden (P403, mynnar i); där Wikidata anger flera ger kortet det hav eller den vik som även de andra källorna nämner, och en anteckning nämner det mindre vattnet." | fixed |
| deck | The English selection named the Finnish rivers and the Torne by Swedish forms that differ from the English fronts; the English description said "Torne älv". | English selection now lists Göta älv, Klarälven, Torne, Kemijoki, Oulujoki, Vuoksi, Kymijoki (and Vuoksi among the rivers into lakes); the English description says "the Torne and the Göta älv". The Swedish description keeps "Torne älv". | fixed |
| st-lawrence | "Saint Lawrencefloden"/"Saint Lawrenceviken" are established (Wikidata sv labels, sv.wikipedia, NE), though Språkrådet's general rule would hyphenate. | Kept; method step 4 now says the unhyphenated NE/Swedish Wikipedia/Wikidata form was preferred over the alias "Saint Lawrence-floden". | no change needed |

### Round 3: Licensing, attribution and documentation (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — independent Licensing, attribution and documentation reviewer · **Scope:** Every source's licence and role, the attribution in the built TTL, the evidence of all 50 cards (22 spot-checked by fetching), the recorded queries and scripts.

Licensing found compliant (CC0 from Wikidata and a US Government work). Fixed: the Wikipedia and Wikidata source URLs pointed at a list page and a property page; the Swedish "Jenisejviken" was undocumented as coming from the Swedish Wikipedia; Murrayfloden; labels.py and cards.py undocumented; NE's usedFor overstated the mouths it confirmed.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| deck | The Wikipedia sources' URLs were the list pages "List of rivers by length" and "Lista över floder", which were not used and suggest a CC BY-SA selection; the TTL repeated them in prov:used. | URLs set to https://en.wikipedia.org/ and https://sv.wikipedia.org/; the per-card revision locators are kept; rebuilt. | fixed |
| yenisei | The note's Swedish "Jenisejviken" is not in Wikidata (Q1338198 has no sv label or alias, confirmed today) but comes from the Swedish Wikipedia, which was described as "Nothing copied". | Method step 4, the yenisei Wikidata evidence, the wikipedia-sv and wikidata usedFor and the licensing now say the name is taken from the Swedish Wikipedia article "Jenisej"; a single place name is a fact, not protected by copyright, so the source stays verification only and the deck CC0. | fixed |
| darling | The Swedish back "Murray" breaks the deck's stated alias rule; NE says "Murrayfloden". | Changed to "Murrayfloden" (see round 1); Murrayfloden added to method step 4 and to the licensing paragraph. | fixed |
| deck | cards.py, labels.py and make_dossier.py were not recorded. | labels.py appended verbatim to query 3's record; method step 5 says what the card table cards.py holds (only values that appear in the dossier); method step 8 says make_dossier.py assembled the dossier from cards.json and the written text. | fixed |
| deck | NE's usedFor ("the mouth (48 of the 50 rivers …)") reads as if 48 mouths were confirmed, but the visitor opening names no mouth for 8 rivers. | Reworded: Swedish names checked for 48 rivers; the mouth, or the wider water it is part of, confirmed for 40, with the 8 exceptions named (counted from each card's NE evidence). | fixed |
| deck | The Wikidata source URL was the property page of P403, narrow for a source that also gives labels and other statements. | URL set to https://www.wikidata.org/; P403 stays in the title. | fixed |

### Round 5: Final full-deck review (facts and language) (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — independent final reviewer · **Scope:** All 50 cards (every P403 and label check re-run against live Wikidata, en/sv/mul), the description, keywords, study direction, selection and method, and every fix logged in rounds 1–4.

No errors or warnings; every fix from rounds 1–4 is in place. Two optional suggestions, both applied: the Elbe note now names its subject, and the selection says the Ural lies on the conventional Europe–Asia boundary.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| elbe | The backNote "Its estuary opens into the German Bight" / "Dess mynningsvik öppnar sig mot Tyska bukten" sits under the back "North Sea", so "Its"/"Dess" can be read as the North Sea's estuary rather than the Elbe's. | Agreed; the fact itself is unchanged (the card's Wikidata evidence lists Q321837 German Bight among the Elbe's P403 values). Note reworded to "The Elbe's estuary opens into the German Bight" / "Elbes mynningsvik öppnar sig mot Tyska bukten", edited in the dossier after the recorded card-building script (whose NOTE_FIX still shows the earlier wording). Rebuilt. | fixed |
| deck | The selection counts the Ural among the "13 in the rest of Europe", but the Ural is the conventional Europe–Asia boundary along much of its course and ends in Kazakhstan, so calling it European is a convention. | Agreed (the Ural card's NE and Swedish Wikipedia evidence say it flows from Russia through Kazakhstan to the Caspian Sea). The selection now lists "and the Ural, conventionally counted as the Europe–Asia boundary along much of its lower course". The card and the description ("every continent except Antarctica") are unaffected. | fixed |
